column1: # Reise 1 and Reise 2 (#237): what a traveller in Japan needs first, as two
# topics inside Kaishi — Henning, 2026-09-19: "als Thema unterhalb von
# Kaishi", no deck of its own, in rounds that stay small enough to finish.
# Two kinds of row, read by import/lib/travel.js:
#   staffel<TAB>id<TAB>word
#     A Kaishi card, by its note id (words repeat in Kaishi, ids do not). The
#     word is only here so a person can read the file; the import checks it.
#     These have Kaishi's native-speaker recordings.
#   staffel<TAB>id<TAB>word<TAB>reading<TAB>meaning<TAB>topics
#     A card Kaishi does not have, added to the Kaishi deck with an id from
#     9_000_000_000_000 up (Kaishi's note ids are ~1.7e12, the kana decks'
#     ~1e7, hers are negative). The Japanese and the English are copied
#     from the Wikivoyage Japanese phrasebook (CC BY-SA 3.0,
#     https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Japanese_phrasebook), where a slash
#     between two variants was split and only one kept — nothing written by a
#     model. The reading is written as it is said, a space between words and
#     the particles は/を as わ/お, because she reads romaji: toRomaji() of it
#     is what the card shows ("toire wa doko desu ka", not "toirehadokodesuka").
#     These start with the generated voice (VOICEVOX, the nightly
#     generate-word-sounds run); a native speaker can record one later from
#     the card's sheet.
#     `topics` (comma-separated, may be empty) are this card's other topics,
#     written by hand: the keyword rules put 6 of these 26 under a wrong
#     topic ("Good morning" under time, "A table for two people, please" under
#     greetings) and 12 under none (measured 2026-09-19), so for these cards
#     the rules are not asked.
#     One reading departs from Wikivoyage's romaji: 行き in この電車はどこ行き
#     is "yuki" there and "iki" in the generated voice (measured 2026-09-19,
#     VOICEVOX audio_query). Both are standard; the reading follows the voice,
#     so the card's romaji never contradicts its own sound.
# Meanings stay English, like the rest of Kaishi.
